players.product: On-site power generation for AI data centers and large loads (Liberty Power Innovations: multi-OEM engine generation stacks with BESS, energy management and ERCOT/PJM market participation)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Michael Stock: Q3 2026 revenue was $1.2 billion, relatively flat with the prior quarter, reflecting strong utilization and a modest pricing uplift, partially offset by drilling-related delays as drilling crews worked to replenish customer well inventory after accelerated completions in Q2; adjusted EBITDA was $142 million. Net loss was $39 million versus net income of $43 million in the prior quarter; adjusted net income was $10 million versus $14 million (excluding $49 million of tax-affected unrealized loss on investments and transaction and other costs); fully diluted net loss per share was 24 cents and adjusted net income per diluted share $0.06 (prior quarter $0.09). G&A was $69 million versus $67 million, including $5 million of stock-based compensation.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 2026 revenue $1.2 billion (relatively flat QoQ); adjusted EBITDA $142 million; net loss $39 million; adjusted net income $10 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ron Gusek: Liberty Power Innovations (LPI) entered into a strategic development agreement earlier this week with 'a leading frontier AI lab' (not named) and a dedicated infrastructure platform (not named) for 1.2 gigawatts of integrated power services at data center campuses. The agreement includes a significant prepayment of capacity fees, targets execution of the first energy service agreement (ESA) for approximately 500 megawatts by December 2026, establishes a phased energization schedule from Q4 2027 through Q1 2029 and includes the substantive commercial terms for the additional long-term ESAs. CEO: it follows months of joint engineering and design of the integrated power architecture for generation, power quality, reliability and dynamic AI load; Liberty is expanding the relationship and already working with the customer on additional projects across other sites, including gas supply, interconnection, permitting and construction planning.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.2 gigawatts; first ESA approximately 500 megawatts targeted by December 2026; energization Q4 2027 through Q1 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity-fee prepayment under the 1.2 GW frontier AI lab agreement: CFO Michael Stock: 'the prepayment is significant ... We think in terms of hundreds of millions of dollars'; it is a prepayment of capacity fees to be amortized over probably the first five years of the contract and 'it will certainly execute before the final ESA is paid' (as transcribed). CEO Ron Gusek: it applies against the 1.2 gigawatts, receipt is expected in the near term and 'It's not contingent on execution of the ESA.' Management: 'The 300 million is not specific to this project. It's a form of commitment from the client for the whole 1.2 gigawatts'; it will be booked on the balance sheet as deferred revenue and be a significant source of cash for the fourth quarter (CFO Michael Stock).
quarterly_data.figure: hundreds of millions of dollars; the 300 million; amortized over probably the first five years

quarterly_data.signal: Path to the first ESA with the frontier AI lab: management said all the major commercial terms are agreed and Liberty is in the final legal drafting of the ESAs, working through the site-specific portions; with a standard ESA for the whole 1.2 gigawatts, later ESAs with this client should be 'rinse and repeat' and only site-specific. CEO Ron Gusek: the ESA contemplates a 15-year term with a renewal opportunity. Management: each ESA attaches to a single data center building (buildings of maybe three, four, five hundred megawatts of IT load at a time), so the remaining capacity follows in phases, building by building, site by site. Management: 'At this point in time, we're confident around our ability to get there' before the end of the year; there is a front-running series of sites in a particular locale plus a couple of backup sites in different states it could pivot to, with possibly a modest delay.
quarterly_data.figure: first ESA targeted by December 2026; 15-year ESA term with renewal

quarterly_data.signal: Power generation capacity: management is 'very confident that we have the 3 gigawatts available to us to execute and have energized by the end of 2029' and has not added or announced any additional capacity. Liberty started taking delivery of generation early and still has inbound supply-chain capacity to allocate for the last part of 2027 ramping through 2028 (conversations for late 2027 / early 2028 are 'very far advanced'); 'just a bit over a gigawatt' will come energized in 2029. Its top eight projects represent significantly more than the three gigawatts of generation available, and those conversations continue to progress.
quarterly_data.figure: 3 gigawatts energized by the end of 2029; just a bit over a gigawatt energized in 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook: CEO Ron Gusek expects Q4 weather and holiday seasonality to be partially offset by continued strength in demand, including activity deferred from Q3; management expects 'a slightly smaller than normal seasonal breakdown for Q4' and sees no budget exhaustion this year. Management declined to give a specific Q4 number. CFO Michael Stock, asked whether the 2026 capex number of one and a half billion dollars given last quarter is still the same: 'Yes, our CapEx guide for the year is still intact. We're not changing that.' CFO: tax expense rate for the rest of 2026 approximately 24% of pre-tax income, with no material cash taxes expected this year. The full 2027 completions outlook will come on the next call (RFP season not yet complete).
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex guide intact (one and a half billion dollars); tax rate approximately 24%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Michael Stock: Q3 net capital expenditures and long-term deposits were $622 million, including approximately $450 million in power generation deposits and other investments in power generation, plus capitalized maintenance spending and other projects. Q3 cash balance was $119 million, net debt $1.2 billion and total liquidity $669 million. Other expense of $69 million included $63 million of unrealized fair value losses on non-core equity investments. CFO: the completions business had positive free cash flow this quarter and every other quarter, and is expected to again next year while reinvesting in the digiPrime fleet.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 net capex and long-term deposits $622 million (approximately $450 million power generation); cash $119 million; liquidity $669 million

quarterly_data.signal: Power project returns: management: 'Nothing has changed there. We continue to target those high teams rates of return' (as transcribed, on invested capital); total deployed capital per project depends on balance-of-plant complexity, from a much lower multiple of generation cost for a basic commercial or industrial project up towards two times the cost of generation for a very complex inference data center with a volatile load profile. CFO Michael Stock: Liberty is still targeting 'around 5 times cash on cash payback' (as transcribed) - 'The 15-year, we're at that five', while a 20-year contract 'might move out towards the six-year mark'; when Liberty undertakes extended scope for a client, 'we do not dilute our capital returns'.
quarterly_data.figure: 'those high teams rates of return' (as transcribed); up towards two times the cost of generation; 15-year contract 'at that five'; 20-year contract towards the six-year mark

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ron Gusek: LPI recently completed advanced grid integration testing with the National Laboratory of the Rockies Controllable Grid Interface, connecting LPI's physical generation assets and TEMPO controls to a synthetic grid modeled on a specific real-world electric system in the southern United States. The testing demonstrated grid operability and expected changes over the life of an islanded-to-grid participating project and validated Liberty's control methodology and compliance with applicable IEEE standards; CEO: the results advance its ability to coordinate on-site generation with the grid, including capabilities such as peak shaving (a test, not a commercial deployment).

Wyoming site: management said Liberty has just initiated the large load permit for its Wyoming site (a permitting timeline of generally about 16 to 18 months); the earliest the project would start is the back end of 2028 into 2029 and 2030, and the data center partner on the site will market it to hyperscalers before Liberty partners with the final hyperscaler. Management referred to 'the 1.9 gigawatts in Wyoming' and said Liberty is building a pipeline of projects into the 2030s as 'a multi-gigawatt non-geographic specific IPP'.
quarterly_data.figure: 16 to 18 month permitting; 1.9 gigawatts in Wyoming; earliest start back end of 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ron Gusek on the power customer base: hyperscalers seeking co-located power are new to this world and want partners covering everything from the gas molecule, its interconnection and contracting, through design, construction and operation of the power plant and a balance of plant with power quality systems for volatile data center load, to grid integration and commercial grid participation. Management: to limit risk, Liberty engages with a number of end customers and hyperscalers and holds access to sites in a range of states and counties, so that no single decision in one state or locale would meaningfully affect the business.

Completions (frac) operations: CEO Ron Gusek: record natural gas substitution of over 60% of the total fuel consumed by Liberty's fleets provided annualized fuel savings equating to over $1 billion for its customers. Moving a customer from a diesel fleet to a natural gas fleet can enable maybe 50 million dollars a year in annualized savings at today's arbitrage, letting Liberty ask for a price that earns a return on invested capital ('We've always said we want to lessen a three-year cash on cash payback', as transcribed); digiPrime fleet pricing is more resilient than diesel fleets, with dual-fuel in between. Management: Q3 drilling-related delays came from catching up to drilling rigs after Q2's work through uncompleted well inventory, calling it 'a bit of a singularity' rather than a recurring issue.
quarterly_data.figure: natural gas substitution over 60%; annualized customer fuel savings over $1 billion; maybe 50 million dollars a year in annualized savings from moving a customer from a diesel to a natural gas fleet

quarterly_data.signal: Management on the frac market and 2027: the rig count increase has supported demand for probably of order 15 to 18 incremental frac crews and a relatively tight frac market — 'Our calendar is full' — allowing modest pricing increases quarter on quarter; with the forward oil curve strengthened (2027 above $85, 2028 above 70, maybe even above 75) management is 'feeling more confident about our ability to go and get some additional price as we head into 2027', though not a return to mid-cycle economics. CEO Ron Gusek: RFP season is well advanced and Liberty already knows the homes for most of its fleets for 2027, some renewed without an RFP. Management expects continued inflationary headwinds, especially labor and trucking ('directly influenced by the whole data center build'), after tariff and fluids increases that have mostly stabilized, partly offset by digiPrime component longevity and AI software monitoring. CEO: Liberty will keep investing in next-generation equipment at a reasonable cadence amid strong demand for it.
quarterly_data.figure: 15 to 18 incremental frac crews; 2027 forward curve above $85; 2028 above 70
